jobs.title: Senior Director, Pharmacy Experience and Transformation
jobs.description:
Location:

243 Consumers Road, Toronto, Ontario, M2J 4W8

At Shoppers Drug Mart, we’re innovating health and wellness in Canada. From prescriptions to walk-in clinics, and a beloved loyalty program, we’re caring and supporting our customers in new ways every day.

With more than 1,300 locally owned and operated stores from coast to coast, the Shoppers Drug Mart network is more than a great place to shop, it’s a great place to work. We’re committed to building our talented team who champion collaboration, kindness and inclusivity. Join our team, and help recognize a healthy future for your career and for all Canadians.

Why this role is important?

Reporting to the VP, Pharmacy Operations, Clinical Excellence and Transformation, the Senior Director, Pharmacy Experience and Transformation will lead the strategy and execution of transformational initiatives shaping the future of pharmacy at Shoppers Drug Mart.

This role will own the pharmacy AI, technology, automation and optimization agenda
, while ensuring that the patient and pharmacy team experience remains at the centre of transformation. The successful candidate will identify and scale opportunities that improve how patients access and experience pharmacy care, simplify pharmacy workflows, enhance team member experience and deliver measurable operational and business value.

Working closely with Pharmacy Operations, Technology, Digital, Clinical Excellence, and other cross-functional partners, this leader will translate emerging capabilities, patient and team insights, and business opportunities into a clear transformation strategy and roadmap. They will be comfortable operating at both the strategic and execution level, taking initiatives from early-stage discovery and business case development through implementation, adoption, and scale.

What You’ll Do

Define and lead the Pharmacy Experience and Transformation strategy and roadmap, with a strong focus on AI, automation, technology and the evolving needs of patients and pharmacy teams.
Own the pharmacy AI agenda, identifying and prioritizing opportunities to apply AI and emerging technologies to improve patient experience, pharmacy workflows, team member experience and operational performance.
Lead a portfolio of key transformation initiatives, including Experience Insights & Analysis, Pharmacy Experience Program (PEP), Rx Delivery, AI Call Agent and Assisted Data Entry.
Translate strategic opportunities into scalable solutions, leading initiatives from discovery, concept development and business case through implementation, adoption and value realization.
Champion a patient- and team-centred approach to transformation, ensuring new technology and process changes make pharmacy interactions simpler, more seamless and more meaningful.
Identify opportunities to redesign, simplify and automate pharmacy workflows, reducing administrative burden and enabling pharmacy teams to spend more time supporting patients and delivering care.
Use patient feedback, pharmacy team insights, operational data, market trends and emerging technology to identify opportunities and shape the future pharmacy experience.
Partner closely with Pharmacy Operations, Technology, Digital, Clinical Excellence and other teams to align business priorities, technology capabilities and investment against the transformation roadmap.
Lead experience discovery and analysis to better understand patient and team member pain points, unmet needs and emerging expectations, and translate those insights into actionable transformation priorities.
Establish clear success measures across patient experience, pharmacy team experience, operational performance and financial value, and monitor outcomes to ensure initiatives are delivering meaningful impact.
Build alignment across senior stakeholders and cross-functional teams, bringing clarity and structure to complex transformation opportunities and driving decisions required to move initiatives forward.
Lead and develop a high-performing team with a strong culture of strategic thinking, innovation, experimentation, accountability and execution.

What You’ll Need

Senior leadership experience in strategy, AI, digital transformation, technology, customer experience or large-scale business transformation.
Demonstrated ability to develop transformation strategies and take complex initiatives from concept and business case through implementation and scale.
Strong understanding of AI, automation and emerging technologies, and how they can be applied to improve customer or patient experience, frontline workflows and operational efficiency.
Strong strategic thinking and problem-solving skills, with the ability to bring structure and direction to complex or ambiguous opportunities.
A strong human-centred mindset, with demonstrated ability to translate patient, customer and frontline team needs into meaningful experience improvements.
Strong business acumen, including the ability to assess opportunities, build compelling business cases and connect transformation investments to measurable value.
Proven ability to lead complex, cross-functional initiatives across operations, technology, digital and business teams.
Strong executive communication, stakeholder management and influencing skills, with the ability to align senior leaders around a transformation agenda.
Experience using data, insights and performance measures to inform strategy, prioritize opportunities and assess impact.
Experience in pharmacy, healthcare, retail, technology, consulting or another complex operating environment.
Demonstrated ability to lead and develop high-performing teams through significant change and transformation.
Post-Secondary education in Industrial or Process Engineer / Technology / Business/ Healthcare or Operations
7-10 years' experience, retail preferred
MBA or relevant advanced degree is an asset.
Must be available to travel across Canada as required.

Why work at Shoppers Drug Mart?

Acting as consultants, supporting internal customers and the Associate-Owners, you will get experience unique to the retail industry while working for an award-winning national brand. Benefit from a purchase discount program, competitive pay and online learning through Academy .

Take ownership of your work and find more ways to care about your work, co-workers, customers and community.

How You’ll Succeed

At Shoppers Drug Mart Inc., we seek great people to continually strengthen our culture. We believe great people model our values, are authentic, build trust and make connections.

If that sounds like you, and you are open-minded, responsive to change and up to the challenges provided in a fast-paced retail environment, apply today.

Employment Type

Full time

Type Of Role

Regular

Shoppers Drug Mart Inc. recognizes Canada's diversity as a source of national pride and strength. We have made it a priority to reflect our nation’s evolving diversity in the products we sell, the people we hire, and the culture we create in our organization. Accommodation is available upon request for applicants with disabilities in the recruitment and assessment process and when hired.

In addition, we believe that compliance with laws is about doing the right thing. Upholding the law is part of our Code of Conduct – it reinforces what our customers and stakeholders expect of us.

Description de poste:

Director, Enterprise Architecture Strategy, Core Platform

The Director, Enterprise Architecture Strategy is the architecture strategist supporting the Assistant Vice President, Enterprise Architecture, Core Platforms.

The Director drives the architecture integration strategy across cloud, on premise, network, application platforms, and foundational technology services. The role translates enterprise and business priorities into actionable architecture direction, roadmaps, investment priorities, standards, and modernization outcomes.

Working closely with the AVP, other Enterprise Architects, technology executives, engineering leaders, and domain and solution architects, the Director ensures that architecture priorities are aligned with business, operational, security, regulatory, and cost outcomes.

What will you do?

Working in collaboration with the other Enterprise Architects, define future-state architectures, transition roadmaps, principles, standards, reference architectures, and decision boundaries.
Provide strategic analysis, recommendations, visibility and executive reporting into architecture decisions, investments, dependencies, risks, and outcomes.
Maintain an integrated view of architecture priorities, decisions, dependencies, and outcomes.
Translate business priorities, executive direction, regulatory obligations, operational risks, and technology constraints into actionable architecture priorities.
Integrate cloud, infrastructure, network, security, identity, platform, API, and application architecture into a coherent enterprise direction.
Facilitate joint architecture planning and decision-making where initiatives cross business, portfolio, or technology boundaries.
Promote the reuse of enterprise capabilities, platforms, standards, patterns, and architecture decisions.
Escalate unresolved cross-domain decisions to the appropriate architecture or executive authority.
Lead architecture governance and ensure architecture decisions are documented, traceable, implementable, and aligned with security, resilience, operational, financial, and compliance requirements.
Partner with engineering and operational leaders to validate that architecture direction is practical, financially responsible, and sustainable in production.
Define and communicate measurable outcomes for technology health, risk reduction, resilience, cost efficiency, simplification and platform adoption.

What you'll need to succeed?

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, Business Technology Management, or a related discipline. A master’s degree is preferred.
Enterprise architecture credentials such as TOGAF, IASA CITA, or an equivalent architecture certification are preferred.
10 or more years of progressive architecture experience, including enterprise, portfolio, or cross-domain responsibility.
Demonstrated experience developing enterprise technology strategies, future-state architectures, integrated roadmaps, standards, and transition plans.
Broad knowledge of cloud platforms, networks, operating systems, middleware, identity, security, virtualization, application hosting, APIs, integration, automation, and platform engineering.
Experience with cloud migration, infrastructure transformation, vulnerability remediation, technology currency, lifecycle management, and technical debt reduction.
Experience integrating architecture strategies and resolving dependencies across multiple business and technology domains.
Proven ability to influence senior business and technology leaders through clear analysis, options, trade-offs, and recommendations.
Ability to translate business and enterprise priorities into actionable architecture direction.
Ability to synthesize complex and fragmented information into a coherent enterprise position.
Excellent executive communication, facilitation, negotiation, and influence.
Strong financial and analytical acumen, including investment, cost, risk, and value trade-offs.
Ability to lead through influence, establish decision clarity, and resolve conflicts.
Sound judgment regarding when to standardize, consolidate, modernize, remediate, replace, retire, or accept risk.

What’s in it for you?

A competitive salary and bonus program, based on market scale
A flexible group insurance program starting on your first day of work to meet your needs and those of your family.
Time off that allows you to focus on the moments that matter most. 20 vacation days per year.
Our Share Ownership Program gives you the opportunity to invest in Sun Life while benefiting from employer matching contributions.
We are proud to be included in Great Place to Work's 2026 list of Canada's Best Workplaces.
Working together, sharing common values, and encouraging growth & achievement.

Description de poste:

Director, Domain Enterprise Architect, RPA and Intelligent Automation

Reporting to the Assistant Vice President, Enterprise Architecture, Core Platforms, the Director, Domain Enterprise Architect, RPA and Intelligent Automation leads the architecture for Sun Life’s Intelligent Automation platforms.

The Director defines the RPA and Intelligent Automation domain strategy, future-state architectures, standards, reference architectures, and technology roadmaps. The scope includes RPA, Intelligent Document Processing, Microsoft Power Platform, process mining, workflow orchestration, and Agentic AI capabilities applied to business process automation.

Working with business leaders, Technology Executives, other Enterprise Architects, application development teams, AI platform teams, security, privacy, operations, and engineering groups, the Director aligns Intelligent Automation investments and architecture decisions with business priorities, regulatory obligations, operational requirements, and measurable outcomes.

What will you do?

Define and maintain the RPA and Intelligent Automation domain architecture strategy, principles, standards, and technology roadmaps.
Assess the current-state RPA and Intelligent Automation architecture to identify capability gaps, risks, redundant technologies, technical debt, and opportunities for consolidation or modernization.
Define future-state architectures for RPA, intelligent document workflows, low-code automation, process mining, workflow orchestration, AI-assisted operations, and Agentic AI capabilities applied to business processes.
Establish architecture patterns, guardrails, decision frameworks, and reference architectures that enable secure, scalable, resilient, auditable, and production-ready Intelligent Automation capabilities.
Collaborate with business leaders and Technology Executives to communicate architecture direction, options, trade-offs, investment considerations, risks, and expected outcomes for RPA and Intelligent Automation.
Drive platform standardization, reusable automation patterns, and approved citizen and professional development approaches to reduce duplication and improve delivery efficiency.
Collaborate with Enterprise, Domain, Solution, Application, Data, Cloud, Infrastructure, Security, Privacy, and AI Platform Architects to align automation decisions and resolve cross-domain dependencies.
Lead RPA and Intelligent Automation domain architecture governance, including architecture reviews, risk assessments, exception management, and architecture decision records, ensuring alignment with security, privacy, responsible AI, resilience, operational, regulatory, and compliance requirements.

What you’ll need to succeed?

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related discipline. A master’s degree is preferred.
Enterprise architecture credentials such as TOGAF, IASA CITA, or an equivalent architecture certification are preferred.
Relevant certifications in RPA, Microsoft Power Platform, workflow automation, process mining, AI, security, or related technologies are considered assets.
10 or more years of progressive architecture experience, including enterprise, domain, portfolio, application, or platform architecture responsibility.
Significant experience designing, governing, and modernizing enterprise RPA, Intelligent Automation, workflow, or business process technology platforms.
Deep expertise in at least one major Intelligent Automation capability and broad knowledge across RPA, Intelligent Document Processing, Microsoft Power Platform, process mining, workflow orchestration, Generative AI, and Agentic AI integration patterns.
Demonstrated experience defining RPA and Intelligent Automation architecture strategies, future-state architectures, technology roadmaps, standards, reference architectures, and governance practices.
Proven ability to collaborate with Technology Executives and influence senior business and technology leaders through clear analysis, architecture options, trade-offs, risks, and recommendations.
Strong strategic thinking with the ability to translate business priorities, executive direction, regulatory obligations, operational risks, and technology constraints into actionable RPA and Intelligent Automation architecture direction.
Knowledge of AI governance, AI risk management, responsible AI principles, privacy requirements, and enterprise AI adoption patterns as they apply to Intelligent Automation.
Ability to assess automation requirements and determine the appropriate platform, integration pattern, architecture approach, governance controls, and delivery boundaries.
Strong financial and analytical acumen, including investment prioritization, value realization, platform rationalization, technical debt, risk, and technology portfolio trade-offs.

What’s in it for you?

A competitive salary and bonus program, based on market scale
A flexible group insurance program starting on your first day of work to meet your needs and those of your family.
Time off that allows you to focus on the moments that matter most. 20 vacation days per year.
Our Share Ownership Program gives you the opportunity to invest in Sun Life while benefiting from employer matching contributions.

Working together, sharing common values, and encouraging growth & achievement.

jobs.title: Senior Director Finance
jobs.description:
Senior Director of Finance

Markham, Ontario

Our client is a successful, privately held Canadian company with a well-established business and an entrepreneurial, growth-oriented culture. They are looking for a Senior Director of Finance to join their leadership team and take on a broad, highly visible mandate.

This is not a traditional accounting-focused finance role. While ensuring strong financial discipline remains important, the real opportunity is to become a strategic and commercial partner to the business — helping leadership better understand performance, identify opportunities and make stronger, data-driven decisions.

The Opportunity

Reporting to the President, the Senior Director of Finance will lead the finance function while spending significant time working across the organization.
The mandate will include:
Leading financial planning, budgeting, forecasting and performance analysis
Providing meaningful insight into revenue, margins, pricing, costs and profitability
Developing and enhancing KPIs and management reporting
Partnering with operational and commercial leaders to support better decision-making
Evaluating business cases, capital investments and growth opportunities
Identifying opportunities to improve processes, controls and overall efficiency
Leveraging technology, automation and AI to improve the way financial information is produced and used
Ensuring accurate and timely financial reporting and maintaining appropriate financial controls
Leading, developing and mentoring the finance team
Acting as a trusted financial advisor to senior leadership

The Ideal Candidate

You are a CPA
with progressive finance leadership experience and a strong understanding of a manufacturing or similarly operational business.

You bring strong technical fundamentals, but your real strength is your ability to connect the numbers to the business. You are curious, analytical and commercially minded, and you naturally dig beneath financial results to understand what is driving them.
You are equally comfortable rolling up your sleeves and getting into the details as you are sitting with senior leaders and helping shape a decision.

Experience working within a privately held, entrepreneurial or mid-sized organization would be particularly valuable.

Why Consider This Opportunity?

This is an opportunity to join a successful organization where Finance has a meaningful seat at the table. You’ll have the ability to influence how the business operates, improve the tools and information used to make decisions, and help shape the continued evolution of the finance function.

For someone who enjoys building, improving and influencing — rather than simply maintaining — there is a lot to sink your teeth into here.

Work Model:
Predominantly onsite

jobs.description:
Who We Are

At Momentum Financial Services Group, we help people move forward by reimagining how money works for those who need it most. With more than 40 years of experience, we're the team behind Money Mart—Canada's largest non-bank branch network—and a leader in financial solutions for underserved communities.

From short-term loans to money transfers and prepaid cards, we power the products, technology, and operations that connect over a million customers a year to the money they need, when they need it.

At MFSG, we come together across teams and departments to create something bigger than ourselves: solutions that remove barriers and give people access to money they might not get anywhere else. Whether you're solving problems, building systems, or shaping strategy, your work fuels real support for real people.

We've Got You Covered

Our strategy is designed to attract and retain top talent by offering competitive, fair, and performance-driven rewards. We benchmark against the market, recognize strong performance and continuously evolve to meet the needs of our people and our business.

Enjoy the opportunity for a discretionary bonus based on individual performance and company success.

Comprehensive Benefits:
Our benefits include health and dental plans with 100% of the premiums covered. We also offer an Employee Assistance Program to support your mental well-being and provide resources for personal challenges.

Retirement Plans:
Plan for your future with our robust retirement savings options, ensuring you're set for the long haul.

Hybrid Work Environment:

Enjoy reimbursement for tuition assistance and professional development, discounts through Perkopolis and participate in our rewards and recognition programs to celebrate your contributions.

The Job:
Vice President, Enterprise Architecture
What You'll Do

The Vice President, Enterprise Architecture, is responsible for leading Momentum's business and technology on a unified path towards an enterprise target architecture that enables innovation, scalability, and sustainable business growth. This role defines and drives the strategic vision for data, integration, business architecture, and technology platforms —ensuring that architecture and technology investments accelerate business strategy, reduce costs, and position the organization for AI readiness.

What You'll Bring

15+ years of progressive technology leadership in enterprise architecture, data strategy, and platform modernization
Proven experience in rationalizing complex technology environments, reducing technical debt, and delivering measurable cost efficiencies
Demonstrated success leading transformation of large-scale data and technology ecosystems in financial services or similarly regulated industries
Strong track record of building AI- and data-ready enterprise architectures
Experience marrying business architecture with future state architecture

Expertise in enterprise data architecture, governance, and analytics

Strategic ability to balance innovation, performance, and cost optimization

Strong executive communication, influence, and leadership capabilities

Professional Designations (Accreditations, Certificates, Licenses)

The National Director, Tax, Estate & Insurance Planning serves as a national technical resource and thought leader, providing advanced planning expertise, education and consultation to advisors and internal stakeholders across Canada. This role is responsible for delivering guidance on complex tax, estate, wealth transfer and insurance planning strategies while helping establish the organization as a leading source of technical expertise within the Canadian life and health insurance industry.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

Serving as a trusted technical resource for advisors across Canada;
Providing guidance on complex tax, estate, retirement, succession and insurance planning strategies;
Reviewing advanced planning cases and provide independent, product-neutral recommendations;
Developing technical articles, white papers, planning guides and industry commentary;
Creating and delivering presentations, webinars and advisor education programs;
Presenting at conferences, advisor meetings and industry events;
Monitoring legislative and regulatory developments affecting advisors and clients;
Supporting large and complex insurance cases involving business owners, professionals and affluent clients;
Building relationships with advisors, accountants, lawyers and industry professionals; and
Acting as an ambassador and recognized thought leader within the Canadian life and health insurance industry.

QUALIFICATIONS:

Minimum 10 years of experience in advanced planning, tax, estate, insurance, accounting, legal or financial planning roles.
Deep expertise in Canadian taxation and estate planning.
Strong understanding of life insurance and living benefit planning strategies.
Proven public speaking and presentation experience.

Commensurate with experience

jobs.title: Director of Finance And Operations
jobs.description:
Director, Finance & Operations

Toronto | Full-time | In person

About AXL

AXL is an AI venture studio with a mission to flip the script of Canadian innovation—creating great companies that carry Canadian values and innovations to the world.

We are looking for a Director of Finance & Operations to build the financial and operational foundation that will enable AXL to grow.

The Role

This is not a conventional comptroller role. We need an entrepreneurial, systems-minded operator who combines financial discipline with a relentless focus on improving how the organization works.
You will treat AXL’s operations as a product and our team members as its customers. When a process fails, your first response should be to understand why—and then simplify, automate, or redesign it. 

While you should be biased towards action, you will not perform every function yourself. AXL works with bookkeepers, lawyers, accountants, technology providers, and other specialists. You will determine what capabilities are needed, engage the right people and tools, and ensure that their work is timely, integrated, and excellent.

Markham, Ontario

Our client is a successful, privately held Canadian company with a well-established business and an entrepreneurial, growth-oriented culture. They are looking for a Senior Director of Finance to join their leadership team and take on a broad, highly visible mandate.

This is not a traditional accounting-focused finance role. While ensuring strong financial discipline remains important, the real opportunity is to become a strategic and commercial partner to the business — helping leadership better understand performance, identify opportunities and make stronger, data-driven decisions.

Reporting to the President, the Senior Director of Finance will lead the finance function while spending significant time working across the organization.

Leading financial planning, budgeting, forecasting and performance analysis
